cards.text: It's early on the first day of the week, and Jesus has risen from the dead. Now He starts appearing to people. Friend, pull up a stool, because THIS is where the whole story has been heading.

cards.question: Who does the risen Jesus appear to first?

cards.text: Mary Magdalene, the woman Jesus had driven seven demons out of. SEVEN. And she's the very first person to see Him risen.

cards.question: After Mary Magdalene sees the risen Jesus, she keeps the news to herself.
Mary goes to tell the people who had been with Jesus, and she finds them ___ and weeping.

cards.text: So Mary brings them the news. Jesus is ALIVE, and she has SEEN Him.

cards.question: When Jesus' followers hear from Mary that He's alive and she has seen Him, they believe it right away.

cards.text: They don't believe it. That's like texting the group chat "I just got promoted!" and everybody fires back "Screenshot or it didn't happen."
After this, Jesus appears again. This time it's to two of them, walking along in the country.

cards.question: When Jesus appears to the two walking in the country, He appears in a different form.
The two go back and report it to the rest. How do the rest react?

answers.text: They do not believe them either
They run out to find Jesus

cards.text: Later, as the Eleven, Jesus' closest disciples, are eating, Jesus appears to them Himself. And oh, He has some words for this room.

cards.question: What does Jesus rebuke the Eleven for?

answers.text: Their unbelief and hardness of heart
Arguing about who was the greatest

cards.question: Jesus rebukes the Eleven for not believing someone. Who?

answers.text: Those who had seen Him after He rose
The prophets who wrote about Him long ago
The angel who spoke at the empty tomb

cards.text: They wouldn't believe the people who SAW Him. That's like a coworker yelling "FREE COOKIES in the break room!" and you just sitting there going "Mm-hm. Sure." while everybody else walks back chewing.
Jesus isn't finished with the Eleven. After the rebuke comes the mission, friend, and He's about to hand them a job.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Eleven to go into all the ___ and preach the gospel to every creature.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them what's riding on this message.

cards.question: According to Jesus, who will be saved?
Jesus also says that whoever does not believe will be condemned.

cards.text: Then Jesus says signs will accompany those who believe. And this list is NOT small.

cards.question: What's the first sign Jesus says believers will do in His name?

cards.text: The list keeps going: new tongues, picking up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it won't harm them. Friend, I JUMP when the oven timer goes off.

cards.question: Jesus says that when believers lay their hands on the sick, the sick will be made well.

cards.text: After the Lord Jesus has spoken to them, He is taken up into heaven. Friend, every single hair on this mustache is standing straight UP.

cards.question: Once Jesus is taken up into heaven, where does He sit down?

answers.text: At the right hand of God

cards.question: With Jesus taken up into heaven, what do the Eleven do?
Once Jesus is taken up, the Lord leaves the Eleven to do the preaching on their own.

cards.text: The Lord works through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompany it. The same room that wouldn't believe the news is now carrying it EVERYWHERE, friend, and if that doesn't preach, nothing does.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'dancing' and 'sleeping' clash with 'and weeping' in the same sentence, so neither is believable. The blank becomes a giveaway instead of a real choice.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: Mark 16:9-20 is missing from some of the earliest manuscripts, and the BSB marks it with a note. The walkthrough tells it as the plain ending of Mark without mentioning this. The docs don't say whether Papa Dorin should acknowledge a text-critical note like this one or ignore it.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin say anything about the manuscript note on Mark 16:9-20 (and on similar passages like John 7:53-8:11)? If so, where should it go (the opening card, a pop-up or nowhere), and how should it be worded?
